pr.title: Label a pull request reviewing as project review run starts its agent, not a minute later at the agent's setup
pr.head: 5b0acdc1ad67b771017115b07ce8c0cd67627486

summary: When a pull request is reviewed in GitHub Actions, project review run starts an agent that runs the review-pr skill with nobody watching. The reviewing label is how the pull-request list shows that a review is under way. Until now, only the agent's own project review setup added that label, and the agent spends most of its first minute reading the skill and the repository before it gets there. So a pull request looked idle for about 70 seconds after its job started.

This change makes project review run add the label itself, after its refusal checks pass and just before it starts the agent, which happens at about 17 seconds into the job. Because the label now goes on before any review exists, the run also has to take it off in cases where nothing else would: the agent could not start, it stopped before its setup, or the run was interrupted. The start comment still comes from the agent's setup.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• reviewing label: the label that marks a pull request whose review is in progress.
  • Start comment: the comment the agent's setup posts when a review begins. While it is live, it means a review is in progress.
  • clear_reviewing: removes the label unless a live start comment still means a review is in progress.
  • review.labels = false: the setting that turns off every label change a review command makes.

cards.title: Who takes the label off
cards.html:
How the run endsWho removes reviewing
The agent publishes a verdictThe agent's publish
The agent set a review up but published nothingreview.finish, as before
The agent could not start, or stopped before setupThe run, through clear_reviewing (new)
The run is interrupted while the agent runsThe run, through clear_reviewing, and then it re-raises (new)

groups.title: Labeling from the run
groups.kicker: Where project review run adds the label and takes it off again
intro: run in run.py is the whole CI review. It reads the pull request and refuses forks, drafts, closed pull requests, and heads this model already reviewed. Then it starts the agent and checks afterward that a verdict was published. The new label edit sits between those two steps, inside the same try as the agent's start. That placement means every refusal returns before the label goes on, and an exception after the label goes on can still take it off.

To make the label edit and the failure comment use one credential, the reviewer's token is now read once, before anything starts, rather than only on the failure path. label_lines, which turns a label change into output lines, moves from cli.py to review.py so that run.py can print the same lines setup prints.

checks.text: The label edit uses change_labels, the same helper setup uses. That helper creates a missing label, skips a label that is already present, and turns a GitHub refusal into a warning rather than an error, so a refused label never stops the review.

files.note: The run adds reviewing before it starts the agent, and removes it when the agent set no review up or the run is interrupted.

checks.text: Every early return and refusal in run comes before this line, so a fork, a draft, a closed pull request, or an already-reviewed head never gets the label. I traced each one, and test_a_refused_run_adds_no_label covers the four refusals.

The handler catches BaseException so that an interrupt, such as a cancelled Actions job's SIGINT, takes the label off and then re-raises. If the agent had already posted its start comment, clear_reviewing leaves the label on.

This branch runs only when the agent set no review up. When it did set one up, review.finish above already removes the label, so neither path removes it twice. I read both branches against set_up_here.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: When the label goes on, what keeps it off, and what takes it off
intro: The fake gh in tests/test_run.py now handles gh pr edit and label creation. For each edit, it records whether the agent process had started yet, so a test can tell that the label went on before the agent ran rather than through the agent's own setup.

files.note: Covers labeling before the agent starts, no label on a refused run, review.labels = false, a refused edit, and label removal on every failure path, interrupt included.
Checks that setup makes no second label edit when the run already added reviewing.

files.note: The review run section adds the label step, the cleanup, and closed pull requests to the list of refusals.
Steps 4 and 5 of the job describe the early label and when it comes off.

checks.text: The 17-second figure is when the agent started in the measured run, not a label anyone has observed yet. The pull request body says the first CI review after the merge will confirm it. The review lists rewording this as a suggestion.
